items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: He's like Cindy Bessier, you know.

ctx.x: Buddy Petit. Yeah. I say he used to make some peculiar chords, didn't he?

Oh, yeah. Yeah. He's like Cindy Bessier, you know. He used to make the chords, Paul Woodman, ain't he? He said he couldn't like the music that Cindy Bessier made. John Rovershoe said that too. Yeah. And he used to play an old broken chord, get the melody out of it. Pack it up with paper like this, cigarette paper, his pads, you know. Did you work with, uh, you know, a little bit of a melody out of it? Mm-hm. Did you work with, uh, Be Cher much? and get the melody out of it. Pack it up with paper like this,…
Did you work with Bechet much? Did you play banjo with Bechet?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: The amount that I learned good when I used to play with Clarence Williams, you know. Piano, manolene, violin, and sax. That was Cindy Bessier.

ctx.x: Who did he play with? Just some fellas down there. I wasn't playing music then, you know. He'd play class, you know, victory balls, you know. All of them trunks, you know. I don't know. I could play manolene a little bit. The amount that I learned good when I used to play with Clarence Williams, you know. Piano, manolene, violin, and sax. That was Cindy Bessier. Yeah, he was, Cindy was a good thing. Cindy was a good thing. Cindy used to play with anybody too. You know, when he was cold out. Yeah, he didn't have…
He's trying to make the sax. He's a drummer.
